judge.reason: It claims an explicit complete classification, identical to e2.

options.counterfactual: The proposed metaplectic detector does not produce a nilpotent quotient of class at most c that retains the required nontrivial central element, so it does not prove strictness for every n ≥ 3 and c ≥ 3.
options.approach: Audit the congruence-filtration argument directly from Steinberg relations, focusing on opposite-root commutators and the compatibility of the deep splitting with conjugation. Identify whether an omitted central factor invalidates the claimed nilpotency bound.

options.counterfactual: The proposed metaplectic detector does not produce a nilpotent quotient of class at most c that retains the required nontrivial central element, so it does not prove strictness for every n ≥ 3 and c ≥ 3.
options.approach: Construct a finite detector independently for n = 4 and c = 3. This would test the first higher-rank instance without relying on the central-extension filtration.

options.counterfactual: The proposed metaplectic detector does not produce a nilpotent quotient of class at most c that retains the required nontrivial central element, so it does not prove strictness for every n ≥ 3 and c ≥ 3.
options.approach: Withdraw the all-rank conclusion and separate the independently verified rank-three witnesses from the unresolved stabilization step. State exactly which cases remain supported after removing the detector.

options.counterfactual: The integral equality A₃(n) = γ₃(IAₙ) fails for some rank, so a pair with c = 2 belongs to the requested set.
options.approach: Audit the purported integral degree-two proof, distinguishing a primitive relation lattice from a merely rational spanning result. Locate the first rank where an unproved support reduction or lattice-saturation assertion enters.

options.approach: Recompute degree-two derivation brackets and genuine group-relation lattices using Smith normal form in small ranks. A nontrivial discrepancy would provide a concrete candidate for a degree-two kernel class.

options.counterfactual: The integral equality A₃(n) = γ₃(IAₙ) fails for some rank, so a pair with c = 2 belongs to the requested set.
options.approach: Reformulate the classification conditionally on integral degree-two injectivity and remove the exclusion of c = 2. Explain what explicit element or integral theorem is needed to settle that boundary.

options.counterfactual: Some rank-three Johnson-kernel classes become trivial in the lower-central graded quotient after adding free generators, despite remaining nontrivial as automorphisms.
options.approach: Compare the rank-three and rank-four classes using genuine relations in the larger IA group. An explicit expression as a product of weight-(c + 1) commutators would demonstrate that stabilization kills the class.

options.approach: Check whether the all-rank Alexander representation detects the same witness independently of the rank-three quotient. This would distinguish failure of a particular stabilization argument from failure of the proposed classification.

options.counterfactual: Some rank-three Johnson-kernel classes become trivial in the lower-central graded quotient after adding free generators, despite remaining nontrivial as automorphisms.
options.approach: Search for witnesses involving all available generators rather than embedding a fixed rank-three word. Their nonmembership in the next lower-central subgroup could require a detector adapted to the full rank.
